passage:
Gargi: manager just gave you the Kolkata account as well?
Harish: yep. third new account this quarter 😅
Harish: everyone else "has a lot on"
Gargi: you have three accounts and Nikhil has one
Harish: I know. but she said "you are the only one I trust with this"
Harish: and I hate that it makes me feel taller
Gargi: ok that's honest
Harish: I do feel used. also kind of proud. both at once
Gargi: want me to come with you when you tell her it's too much?
Harish: maybe. let me think first

qa.q: How many accounts does Harish have compared with Nikhil?
qa.a: Harish has three accounts and Nikhil has one.

qa.q: What mixed feelings does Harish describe about being trusted with the Kolkata account?
qa.a: Harish feels used and also proud at the same time; being trusted feels flattering even though the workload is unfair.

qa.q: What choice does Gargi offer Harish, and why might it help?
qa.a: Gargi offers to come along when Harish tells the manager it is too much, which gives support so that Harish does not have to make the case alone.

qa.q: What might the manager be thinking when handing Harish a third account?
qa.a: The manager probably thinks Harish will always deliver and may not see the total load; the sentence "the only one I trust" suggests relying on reliability without noticing the cost.

grounding: A dependable worker is given extra work because they will always deliver, feeling used but also proud of being needed.

passage: In a small-town post office, Ishita balanced the day's accounts by four, as usual. The postmaster handed her the pension registers as well. "You never make mistakes, Ishita." Deepak, at the next counter, had been on his phone for an hour and was allowed to leave early. Ishita stacked the registers, her jaw tight. She felt used, and yet she stood a little straighter, because the postmaster trusted her. On the way home she rehearsed a sentence to say tomorrow, then dropped it, thinking, they will manage nothing without me.

qa.q: What extra work did the postmaster hand to Ishita?
qa.a: The postmaster handed Ishita the pension registers as well.

qa.q: What mixed feelings does Ishita have while stacking the registers?
qa.a: Ishita feels used, with a tight jaw, and also proud, standing a little straighter at being trusted; the two feelings sit side by side.

qa.q: What could Ishita say tomorrow to keep the trust but reduce the load?
qa.a: Ishita could name what she already handles, show the hours involved, and ask the postmaster to share the pension registers with Deepak.

qa.q: How might Deepak see the afternoon, leaving early while Ishita stays?
qa.a: Deepak may not have thought about the extra load on Ishita at all, or may see leaving early as an easy break; nothing in the scene shows Deepak noticing.

grounding: A dependable worker is given extra work because they will always deliver while others coast, feeling used but also proud of being needed.
